label: projectile
notes: Bookkeeping, not a card line. `multishot` beside it is the pellet count a player reads; this row exists because every stat an upgrade moves needs an entry, and it is deliberately given no `unlock` text so phraseAll drops it every time — the count row is always moving alongside it. Same word as that row on purpose; there is nothing new to write here.

label: enemy
notes: Reads as the tail of a sentence — "Bullets pierce {effect}" — because that is the shape the card has always had.

label: projectile lifetime
notes: André 3000's stat. Names how long everything the seal fires stays in the water — the card reads as a bare {effect}, so this label IS the card ("+25% <label>"). Two or three words, and it has to cover missiles and thrown shells as well as the gun, not just the pebbles.

label: recoil boost
notes: Sits at 0 by default, so recoil *= 1.3 measures as no change at all and {effect} correctly declines to claim one. The label is here for the day the base is raised off zero.

label: of everything you fire
notes: bare: the label is already a whole phrase ("of everything you fire"), so no noun is appended.

label: meter per chum
notes: percentOfOne: the stat is a fraction of a meter, so it reads better as a percentage of the thing it fills than as "+0.15".

label: element
unlock: an element on your shots and strike

label: ricochet
unlock: a chaining ricochet shot

label: orbiting shrimp
notes: Bookkeeping, not a card line — see the note on multishotLevel. `shrimpCount` is the row a player reads; this one is dropped by phraseAll on every card because it carries no `unlock`.

label: sea garlic
unlock: a garlicky aura

label: electric eel
unlock: chain lightning

label: laser eyes
unlock: eye beams

label: starfish

label: seagull
unlock: homing dive-bombers

unlock: an oxygen filled bubble that also traps baddies.

label: Bakalar's boat
unlock: a net full of bombs

label: calamari ring
unlock: rings of fried squid

label: dumbo octopus

label: harp seal

label: oyster blaster

label: octopus grabber

notes: The card that raises this is a STUB — disabled in upgrades.csv, and no system reads the stat yet (see CONFIG.upgrades.dolphinPod). The label is here anyway because npm run test:text fails on a stat without one: the day the card is switched on, its {effect} has to render as English rather than as dolphinPodLevel.

label: mussel barrage
unlock: on perfect strike, launches a bearded barrage of mussel munitions

label: club
unlock: a club in your fin slot.

label: thrown club
unlock: hurled homing clubs on a strike

label: club blast
unlock: every club hit detonates

label: club ice
unlock: chill and freeze your opps

label: club
notes: The Bouncer's four. Percentages rather than a level, because the card is a multiplier on a class rather than a level of anything — there is no "club power 3" to name, only the numbers it moved.

label: sonar teeth
unlock: shots that seek, favouring the biggest body in reach

label: maneater
unlock: a taste for swimmers — every one you eat raises all your damage
notes: Counts stacks and nothing else, deliberately: what a stack is WORTH depends on a running total, which is not visible from inside apply(). See applyDamageScaling in stats.js. That makes `level` the honest kind — {effect} would otherwise have to invent a number, which is the exact failure the measured descriptions exist to prevent.

label: iron lung
unlock: all damage scaling with your maximum oxygen
notes: Same as maneater: worth depends on a stat other cards move (max oxygen), so a measured number here would be a lie. Counts stacks only.

label: bomb damage
notes: What one voicemail bomb hits for. Reads as '+22 ___' on a hover tip beside the boat's other level numbers, so it wants to be short and to name the BOMB rather than the boat. Big Rigz is already folded into the figure.

label: blast radius
notes: How wide the bomb goes off, in world units. Sits next to the damage on the same tip, so the two should not read as the same thing said twice. Splash Zone is folded in. Drop the unit if 'm' is wrong for this game's water.

label: between bombs
notes: Seconds between bomb drops while the boat is sailing. LOWER IS BETTER — the lower column is set, so a level that cuts it renders as a gain rather than a loss. Phrase it so '-0.32s ___' reads right.

label: net depth
notes: How far the net hangs below the surface. This is the ONLY part of the net that grows with level — the mouth is a fraction of the hull and never changes — so the wording must not imply the whole net gets bigger. The card's old desc said '+net size' and was wrong about exactly this.

label: net grip
notes: How hard the net holds. It divides a creature's resistance, so a bigger number drags bigger fish and drags everything faster; it is not a speed and not a size. Abstract quantity with no unit — name it so a bare number reads as a strength.

label: between calls
notes: Seconds before the boat comes round again. LOWER IS BETTER. Pairs with 'between bombs' on the same tip, so the two labels should be tellable apart at a glance — one is how often the boat arrives, the other how often it drops while it is here.

label: direct hit
notes: Damage to whatever the bird lands ON. Sits beside the splash on the same tip and the two must be tellable apart — this one only ever hits the single crab that happened to be under it, which is why it is the smaller half of the card.

label: blast damage
notes: Damage from the explosion, which is what the card is actually for — the run IS the blast. Should read as the bigger, more important of the two damage rows.

label: blast radius
notes: How wide the explosion reaches. Drop the 'm' if that unit is wrong for this game's water — it is used on Bakalar's blast too, so change both together.

label: DPS
notes: What a creature standing in the cloud takes per second. Deliberately a DPS and not a per-tick figure — the 0.25s tick is an implementation detail, and a player is comparing this against every other ability they could take instead.

label: radius
notes: How far the cloud reaches. Sits beside the damage row on the same tip; the point of showing both is that a stack now buys strength as well as size, so neither label should imply it is only one of the two. Same 'm' as the two blast radii — change all three together.

label: dmg
notes: What one bolt hits for. Note the tip's figure is the LEVEL curve only — a storm multiplies it on top (CONFIG.eel.storm), deliberately left out so the number does not change with the weather while a thumb is held down.

label: target
notes: How many bodies one bolt chains through. A count, so it pluralises — 'chains to 5 ___'. Sits beside the reach row and the two must be tellable apart: this is HOW MANY, that is HOW FAR between them.

label: reach
notes: How far a bolt will hop to find the next body. Same 'm' as the blast radii — change them together or not at all.

label: dmg
notes: What the shockwave hits for as it sweeps out.

label: reach
notes: How far the wave travels before it dies. The card's whole existence is its reach, so this is the row that sells it.

label: between waves
notes: Seconds between pulses. LOWER IS BETTER — the column is set, so a level that cuts it reads as a gain. It hits a floor inside the cap and drops off the tip after that.

label: strike damage
notes: What one orca's charge hits for. Big Rigz is folded in.

label: between strikes
notes: Seconds before the pod attacks again. LOWER IS BETTER.

label: charge speed
notes: How fast an orca crosses to its target. Last in the readout's order on purpose — beside damage and cadence it reads as flavour, so the four-row cap drops it first.

label: bubble size
notes: How big a trapped fish's bubble is — which is really how big a fish it can take. The card deals no damage at all, so this and the trap length are the whole of what a stack buys.

label: trap length
notes: How long a fish stays held. Pairs with the bubble size on the same tip; one is what it can catch, the other is how long it keeps it.

label: charmed at a time
notes: How many fish the dumbo can hold charmed simultaneously. A ROUNDED STEP — 1 at stack 1, 2 by stack 4 — so on the picks in between it shows dimmed and unchanged rather than vanishing. Phrase it so it reads sensibly both as a change (+1 ___) and standing still (2 -> 2).

label: charm time
notes: How long a fish stays charmed. The card deals no damage at all, so this and the count are most of what a stack buys.

label: between charms
notes: Seconds before it charms again. LOWER IS BETTER.

label: reach
notes: How far it will look for something to charm. Last in the readout's order, so the four-row cap drops it first.

label: arms
notes: How many fish it can drag at once. Another rounded step — dimmed and unchanged on the picks where it does not tick.

label: arm reach
notes: How far an arm will stretch for a fish.

label: yoink speed
notes: How fast it drags what it has caught. Last in the order — the cap drops it before the two above.

label: mussel
notes: How many go out in one barrage. With the damage row, the whole card.

label: direct damage
notes: What one mussel hits for on contact.

label: splash damage
notes: What the small burst around each hit does. A fraction of the direct hit and last in the order, so the four-row cap usually drops it — it is here so the number exists, not because it needs to be read every time.

label: swing damage
notes: What one connecting swing hits for. The Bouncer's multiplier is already folded in, so this is what YOUR club does rather than a bare one.

label: club size
notes: How far the head sits from the fin — the weapon's whole reach, and with it the arc the swing draws.

label: carom dmg
notes: What a THROWN club hits for as it bounces. It is on this card and not on Hurler because the Driftwood level is what buys it — Hurler's own level only buys how many go out. If that reads oddly on a player who holds Hurler and not Driftwood, that is the game being odd, not the label.

label: bounces
notes: How many bodies a thrown club caroms off before it settles. A rounded step, so it shows dimmed and unchanged on the picks where it does not tick.

label: blast dmg
notes: What the explosion on a club hit does. Independent of the Driftwood level — this card scales entirely on its own.

label: blast radius
notes: How wide it goes off. Splash Zone widens it; the Bouncer deliberately does not.

label: freeze time
notes: How long a body is frozen solid once enough hits have landed. The card deals no damage whatsoever, so this and the slow are the entire output.

label: slow per hit
notes: How much each hit slows a body, as a share of its speed — percentOfOne is set, so 0.06 renders as +6%. Enough of them stack into the freeze above.

label: clubs thrown
notes: How many go out on a FULL charge — a half charge throws fewer, and the card can only honestly promise what a committed release does. This is the whole of what Hurler's own level buys; what the clubs DO belongs to Driftwood.

label: note damage
notes: What one note hits for. Half of the card is the note that charms; the other half is the aura the charmed body drags around. This and 'charm length' are the note's two rows.

label: charm time
notes: How long the biggest nearby enemy fights for you.

label: aura damage
notes: What the ring around a charmed body does. The ledger books this separately and it is roughly SEVEN EIGHTHS of the card's whole output, so it wants to read as the important half.

label: aura radius
notes: How wide that ring is.

label: note rate
notes: Seconds between notes. LOWER IS BETTER. Fifth in the order, so the four-row cap normally drops it.

label: aura length
notes: How long the ring lasts on a body. Sixth in the order — usually dropped by the cap.

label: beam damage
notes: What one cut does.

label: beam
notes: How many beams fire at once. A ROUNDED STEP at 0.34 a level — the second arrives at stack four and a third never does inside the cap — so it shows dimmed and unchanged on the picks between. The single most important thing this card does.

label: reach
notes: How far a beam cuts.

label: between beams
notes: Seconds between firings. LOWER IS BETTER.

label: burn
notes: The lingering damage a cut leaves. Fifth in the order — the small rider, which is the row the four-row cap drops.

label: dmg
notes: What the pearl itself hits for before it bursts.

label: popping boba
notes: How many glowing bomblets a burst throws. A rounded step, so it shows dimmed on the picks where it does not tick.

label: boba size
notes: How wide each bomblet goes off.

label: between pearls
notes: Seconds between shots. LOWER IS BETTER.

label: boba dmg
notes: What one bomblet does. Fifth in the order — the small rider the cap drops.

label: escort
notes: How many seals swim with you. THE COUNT IS THE LEVEL, capped at maxSeals — so a pick really does buy a seal each time until the cap, and only damage after that. The card is numbered per stack and this is why.

label: [DRAFT] ram damage
notes: What one escort's ram hits for. Big Rigz is folded in.

label: [DRAFT] blade damage
notes: What one blade hits for.

label: [DRAFT] blades
notes: How many go out per volley.

label: [DRAFT] volley rate
notes: Seconds between volleys — and it COMPOUNDS rather than stepping, so the tip renders it as a multiplier (x0.95 a level) rather than a subtraction. LOWER IS BETTER; the column is set. The delta is a multiplier (the curve compounds) and the span is the seconds themselves, so the unit has to be on the span or the row reads as two different quantities.

label: [DRAFT] bodies cut
notes: How many bodies one blade passes through. A rounded step, capped at pierceMax.

label: [DRAFT] shuriken damage
notes: What one shuriken hits for.

label: [DRAFT] throw rate
notes: Seconds between throws, compounding — rendered as a multiplier like the razor clam's. LOWER IS BETTER. The delta is a multiplier (the curve compounds) and the span is the seconds themselves, so the unit has to be on the span or the row reads as two different quantities.

label: [DRAFT] shuriken size
notes: How big each one is, which is also how easily it connects.

label: [DRAFT] bodies cut
notes: How many bodies one passes through. Rounded step, capped.

label: [DRAFT] seek range
notes: How far a pebble will look for something to bend toward. The ONLY row this card gets: its level also moves a turn rate and a size bias, and both are facts about the simulation rather than about the pebbles.

label: [DRAFT] damage bonus
notes: How much extra damage the held breath is worth, as a share — percentOfOne is set, so 0.4 renders as +40%. It scales with your MAX OXYGEN, so every Yoga makes this bigger; that is exactly what the card could not say before.

label: [DRAFT] arc chance
notes: How often a shot arcs to a second fish. Capped at chanceMax, so it stops moving before the stack cap does.

label: [DRAFT] arcs
notes: How many bodies one arc reaches. A rounded step.

label: [DRAFT] poison a second
notes: Damage per second while poisoned. THE ONLY THING a venom level buys — its duration and stack cap are flat — which is worth knowing and was invisible before.

label: [DRAFT] slow per hit
notes: How much each shot slows a body, as a share of its speed. Capped at maxSlow. Enough of them stack into the freeze.

label: [DRAFT] freeze length
notes: How long a body stays frozen once the slow tops out.

label: [DRAFT] infection a second
notes: Damage per second while infected.

label: [DRAFT] spread range
notes: How far the infection jumps to the next fish — the thing that makes this element scale with a crowd.

label: [DRAFT] burst damage
notes: What a host's death does to everything near it.
